claims.text: Integrating enhanced free-energy sampling with ab-initio molecular dynamics will enable accurate determination of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in high-entropy alloys.
Integrating enhanced free-energy sampling with ab-initio molecular dynamics will make determination of melting and liquid-phase properties computationally efficient.
High-entropy alloys possess a complex free-energy landscape arising from multielement interactions and phase-transition barriers.
Enhanced free-energy sampling facilitates crossing high-energy barriers during melting.
Crossing melting barriers through enhanced sampling enables detailed capture of latent heat, entropy change, and volume variation at the transition.
Improved sampling of the melting transition leads to more reliable predictions of liquid-phase properties.
The proposed method is expected to predict melting temperatures within a few percent of experimental measurements.
The proposed method will provide quantitative estimates of fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting.
The proposed estimates will be significantly more accurate than those from traditional approaches.
The proposed method will be significantly more computationally efficient than traditional approaches.
Traditional calorimetric techniques have limited throughput for determining high-entropy-alloy melting properties.
Standard ab-initio molecular dynamics suffers from limited throughput and incomplete sampling of the melting transition.
The approach may be less applicable to compositions or conditions far outside typical melting ranges.
Extreme compositional disorder may reduce the applicability of the approach.
Non-equilibrium conditions may reduce the applicability of the approach.
Inert-atmosphere or vacuum high-temperature conditions are representative of operational melting environments.
A discrepancy greater than 10% between simulated and experimental properties across the selected alloys would falsify the efficacy of the proposed approach.
